items.headline: Flood Advisory issued September 1 at 6:20AM AKDT until September 1 at 9:30AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
items.description:
Rain showers continue to move across the area this evening bringing
periods of moderate to heavy rain for the Juneau area. Rainfall
amounts around the Mendenhall Valley show around an inch of rain has
fallen in the last six hours with another quarter of an inch
possible.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Montana Creek near areas near the low water crossing on
Montana Creek Road and near Back Loop Road at the Montana Creek
bridge.

* WHEN...Until 930 AM AKDT.
items.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

items.headline: Frost Advisory issued September 1 at 5:39AM AKDT until September 2 at 9:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Temperatures as low as 28 degrees will result in frost
formation.

* WHERE...Colder locations throughout the Anchorage Bowl and Lower
Matanuska Valley.

* WHEN...Through 9 AM AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Frost could harm sensitive outdoor vegetation. Sensitive
outdoor plants may be killed if left uncovered.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The cold airmass and clear skies observed this
morning are expected again tonight through early Wednesday morning.
Many areas of Anchorage and the Matanuska V
items.instruction: Protect tender plants from the cold.

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 1 at 2:30AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Snow. Total snow accumulations of 3 to 6 inches above
2000 feet and 1 to 3 inches below 2000 feet, with higher amounts
above pass level. Winds could gust as high as 30 mph over
Atigun Pass Tuesday night.

* WHERE...Central/Eastern Brooks Range and Eastern Arctic Coast.

* WHEN...Tuesday September 1st through Wednesday September 2nd.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Gusty winds could lead to
areas of blowing snow which could significantly reduce
visibility.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS..
items.areas: Eastern Beaufort Sea Coast; Central Brooks Range; Romanzof Mountains
items.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. Visit 511.alaska.gov or
call 5 1 1 for the latest road conditions.

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued August 31 at 5:10PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
Strong northwesterly winds have developed across Shelikof Strait
and the waters around southern Kodiak Island. These winds are
resuspending ash from the 1912 Katmai-Novarupta eruption,
causing haze and potentially trace amounts of ash accumulation.
The villages of Karluk, Larsen Bay and Akhiok are most likely to
be impacted.

Those in sensitive groups or with respiratory ailments are
encouraged to avoid or reduce outdoor activity to avoid inhaling
the ash. The winds should weaken and shift brief
